  "one_line_summary": "phonet: pep: fix use-after-free in pep_get_sb()",
  "vulnerability_summary": "pep_get_sb() calls pskb_may_pull() which may relocate skb head data, then dereferences the stale pointer ph obtained before the pull, causing a slab use-after-free read.",
  "vulnerability_pattern": "Code saves a pointer to skb header data, calls pskb_may_pull() which may reallocate and invalidate that pointer, then dereferences the stale pointer afterward.",
  "patch": "commit 0f71f852a96af9685858ce59fda34ecbf85c283d
Author: Breno Leitao <leitao@debian.org>
Date:   Tue Jul 21 01:58:45 2026 -0700

    phonet: pep: fix use-after-free in pep_get_sb()
    
    pep_get_sb() doesn't consider that pskb_may_pull() might have relocated
    the skb data, and continue to access the older pointer, causing UAF.
    
    Reproduced under KASAN:
    
      BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in pep_get_sb+0x234/0x3b0
      Read of size 1 at addr ff11000105510f50 by task repro/157
       pep_get_sb+0x234/0x3b0
       pipe_handler_do_rcv+0x5f7/0xa10
       pep_do_rcv+0x203/0x410
       __sk_receive_skb+0x471/0x4a0
       phonet_rcv+0x5b3/0x6c0
       __netif_receive_skb+0xcc/0x1d0
    
    Refetch the header with skb_header_pointer() after pskb_may_pull(), so
    the possibly stale pointer is no longer dereferenced. There are better
    ways to solve this, but, this is the less instrusive one.
    
    Fixes: 9641458d3ec4 ("Phonet: Pipe End Point for Phonet Pipes protocol")
    Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
    Signed-off-by: Breno Leitao <leitao@debian.org>
    Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260721-phonet_get_sb_uaf-v1-1-95fd7881cc4e@debian.org
    Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/phonet/pep.c b/net/phonet/pep.c
index 706927139393..31b29e3ca7bc 100644
--- a/net/phonet/pep.c
+++ b/net/phonet/pep.c
@@ -55,6 +55,8 @@ static unsigned char *pep_get_sb(struct sk_buff *skb, u8 *ptype, u8 *plen,
 	ph = skb_header_pointer(skb, 0, 2, &h);
 	if (ph == NULL || ph->sb_len < 2 || !pskb_may_pull(skb, ph->sb_len))
 		return NULL;
+	/* pskb_may_pull() may have reallocated the head; refetch ph. */
+	ph = skb_header_pointer(skb, 0, 2, &h);
 	ph->sb_len -= 2;
 	*ptype = ph->sb_type;
 	*plen = ph->sb_len;
"
}

  "vulnerability_pattern": "Code saves a pointer to skb header data, calls pskb_may_pull() which may reallocate and invalidate that pointer, then dereferences the stale pointer afterward.",
  "patch": "commit 0f71f852a96af9685858ce59fda34ecbf85c283d
Author: Breno Leitao <leitao@debian.org>
Date:   Tue Jul 21 01:58:45 2026 -0700

    phonet: pep: fix use-after-free in pep_get_sb()
    
    pep_get_sb() doesn't consider that pskb_may_pull() might have relocated
    the skb data, and continue to access the older pointer, causing UAF.
    
    Reproduced under KASAN:
    
      BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in pep_get_sb+0x234/0x3b0
      Read of size 1 at addr ff11000105510f50 by task repro/157

       pipe_handler_do_rcv+0x5f7/0xa10
       pep_do_rcv+0x203/0x410
       __sk_receive_skb+0x471/0x4a0
       phonet_rcv+0x5b3/0x6c0
       __netif_receive_skb+0xcc/0x1d0
    
    Refetch the header with skb_header_pointer() after pskb_may_pull(), so
    the possibly stale pointer is no longer dereferenced. There are better
    ways to solve this, but, this is the less instrusive one.
    
    Fixes: 9641458d3ec4 ("Phonet: Pipe End Point for Phonet Pipes protocol")
    Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
    Signed-off-by: Breno Leitao <leitao@debian.org>
    Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260721-phonet_get_sb_uaf-v1-1-95fd7881cc4e@debian.org
    Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/phonet/pep.c b/net/phonet/pep.c
index 706927139393..31b29e3ca7bc 100644
--- a/net/phonet/pep.c
+++ b/net/phonet/pep.c
@@ -55,6 +55,8 @@ static unsigned char *pep_get_sb(struct sk_buff *skb, u8 *ptype, u8 *plen,
 	ph = skb_header_pointer(skb, 0, 2, &h);
 	if (ph == NULL || ph->sb_len < 2 || !pskb_may_pull(skb, ph->sb_len))
 		return NULL;
+	/* pskb_may_pull() may have reallocated the head; refetch ph. */
+	ph = skb_header_pointer(skb, 0, 2, &h);
 	ph->sb_len -= 2;
 	*ptype = ph->sb_type;
 	*plen = ph->sb_len;

import re, sys, os, subprocess

root = "snapshots/s03" if False else "."
pull_re = re.compile(r'\b(pskb_may_pull|pskb_pull|__pskb_pull_tail|__pskb_pull|skb_linearize|__skb_linearize|skb_cow|skb_cow_head|skb_unclone|pskb_expand_head|skb_share_check)\s*\(')

cap_re = re.compile(r'^\s*(?:const\s+)?(?:struct\s+)?[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\s*\*\s*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*=\s*(?:\([^)]*\)\s*)?(?:skb|[^;]*skb|[^;]*skb->data|[^;]*skb_header_pointer[^;]*)', re.M)

def functions(src):
    """Yield (start_line, funcname, body) using brace matching, skipping comments/strings roughly."""
    # strip comments and strings while preserving newlines
    def clean(s):
        out = []
        i = 0
        n = len(s)
        in_lc = in_bc = in_str = in_chr = False
        while i < n:
            c = s[i]
            nxt = s[i+1] if i+1 < n else ''
            if in_lc:
                if c == '\n': out.append(c); in_lc = False
                i += 1; continue
            if in_bc:
                if c == '*' and nxt == '/': in_bc = False; i += 2; continue
                if c == '\n': out.append(c)
                i += 1; continue
            if in_str:
                if c == '\\': i += 2; continue
                if c == '"': in_str = False
                i += 1; continue
            if in_chr:
                if c == '\\': i += 2; continue
                if c == "'": in_chr = False
                i += 1; continue
            if c == '/' and nxt == '/': in_lc = True; i += 2; continue
            if c == '/' and nxt == '*': in_bc = True; i += 2; continue
            if c == '"': in_str = True; i += 1; continue
            if c == "'": in_chr = True; i += 1; continue
            out.append(c); i += 1
        return ''.join(out)
    s = clean(src)
    lines = s.split('\n')
    func_start_re = re.compile(r'^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*\(')
    i = 0
    n = len(s)
    while i < n:
        # find next '{' at file scope approximation: track brace depth
        pass
    # simpler: iterate lines, find lines that look like func sig ending with '{'
    idx = 0
    while idx < len(lines):
        line = lines[idx]
        m = re.match(r'^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\s*\(', line)
        if m and '{' in line:
            name = m.group(1)
            # collect until braces balance
            depth = line.count('{') - line.count('}')
            start = idx
            j = idx + 1
            while depth > 0 and j < len(lines):
                depth += lines[j].count('{') - lines[j].count('}')
                j += 1
            yield (start+1, name, '\n'.join(lines[start:j]))  # 1-based start line
            idx = j
        else:
            idx += 1

results = []
for dirpath, dirs, files in os.walk(root):
    if '/.git' in dirpath: continue
    for f in files:
        if not f.endswith('.c'): continue
        p = os.path.join(dirpath, f)
        try:
            src = open(p, errors='ignore').read()
        except: continue
        for (sl, name, body) in functions(src):
            plines = [(i+1, l) for i, l in enumerate(body.split('\n')) if pull_re.search(l)]

                    caps.append((sl+i, m.group(2), l.strip()))
            if len(plines) >= 1 and caps:
                results.append((p, sl, name, plines, caps))

for (p, sl, name, plines, caps) in results:

    for (ln, l) in plines:
        print(f"  PULL l{sl+ln-1}: {l.strip()[:110]}")
    for (ln, var, l) in caps[:12]:
        print(f"  CAP  l{sl+ln-1}: {var} = {l[:110]}")
